messages:
alex: Quick workshop: we need a lean battlecard and a short launch kit for the webinar next Tues. Focus: how our serving choices change economics vs public cloud endpoints. 30m sync?
maria: I can run the battlecard draft. goal: one-line claim, three proof bullets, one objection handler per competitor category (cloud infra, LLM API, self-host runtimes).
owen: I'll take the numbers section. new data from the runtime team: median latency down 40% under bursty traffic with adaptive batching. I'll paste a short table in the doc.
taylor: Webinar hooks two options: 1) "From unpredictable bills to predictable units" (ops/fin buyers) 2) "Ship LLM features with SLOs, not experiments" (engineering). Which do we amplify in paid?
sam: Ops/fin resonates in paid. Engineering angle for organic/dev community. my vote: paid = 1, organic = 2.
alex: agree. Maria: for the one-line claim try: "Control your inference economics without rebuilding ops." keeps it non-technical.
maria: draft claim: "Control inference economics and SLOs across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments." too long?
alex: shorten: "Control inference economics across deployments." we can expand in bullets.
owen: pasted numbers into the shared doc: `p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput @seq256/1024, cost per 1k tokens` and note hardware: A100x2 config for Dedicated baseline. add quantization notes.
taylor: marketing asks: avoid absolute numbers on socials. use relative language on social: "up to 3x lower cost for latency-sensitive workloads" and link to benchmark addendum for details.
sam: routing play: web form should capture "deployment intent" (managed/dedicated/private) + "latency requirement" (p99 ms) + "primary use case". then route: managed->PLG SDR, dedicated/private->AE. should we add auto-trial for managed leads?
alex: yes, auto-trial is key. add an experiment: for managed leads with p99 < 200ms, surface a sandbox with preconfigured low-latency profile. measure conversion.
maria: for objection handlers: cloud infra claim: "We can't match your vendor's scale." reply: "Our routing policies and autoscaling are designed for predictable latency at scale; see case study summary." LLM APIs claim: "Simpler to use their API." reply: "Same API surface but with predictable SLOs and cost control levers." self-host runtime claim: "We give you control but want to own infra." reply: "Private deployment option and VPC control plane let you keep data and infra control."
owen: I'll generate a CSV addendum with the seed prompts and test harness. will include exact configs and run IDs.
taylor: slide flow for webinar: 1) problem (billing/latency surprises) 2) how serving choices matter 3) demo: console + routing policy 4) benchmark highlights + addendum link 5) migration checklist + CTA. aim for <6 slides + demo.
sam: CTA prioritization: 1) start trial sandbox 2) request dedicated eval 3) download benchmark pack. put trial + pack front and center.
launch-bot: reminder: landing page draft due 48h. analytics snippet will be auto-injected at 1769133600.
alex: owners: maria -> battlecard + objections; owen -> benchmark CSV + numbers; taylor -> webinar slides + copy; sam -> inbound routing config + Outreach snippets. I'll assemble the launch kit by EOD tomorrow and ping #sales.
maria: uploading draft battlecard in 30 and will keep it deliberately short (one-pager). include quick scripts for SDR.
owen: uploaded CSV and test notes. call out that results are sensitive to prompt mix.
alyx: minor edit: change "SLOs" in public copy to "service guarantees" for non-technical audiences.
taylor: noted. I'll create two headline options for the landing (short + long) and post here.
sam: outreach snippet (draft): "Hey — noticed you're evaluating inference options. We'd love to show how you can lock in performance and cost predictability. Quick 15?" short and calendar-forward.
alex: perfect. wrap-up: ship battlecard + landing + routing in 48h, webinar rehearsals day before. thanks all.
